# FROZEN HISTORICAL FIXTURE — pmm-wake Step 4a BEFORE the #871 fix (PR #887)

**Do not edit this file to keep a test green. It is a snapshot of history, not
live code.** It reproduces `.claude/skills/pr-monitor-and-manage-wake/SKILL.md`
Step 4a exactly as it stood at commit `87c7434` — the last commit before
`3d5a4f1 fix(skills): make pmm-wake resume fail-closed and reset table digests
(#887)`.

It exists so `pmm-wake-step-4a.test.sh` can run its **discrimination control**
in CI instead of merely asserting one in a comment: the same twelve scenarios
are replayed against this pre-fix block, and the suite fails if the pre-fix
block does *not* misbehave. A regression suite that passes against both the
buggy and the fixed code is rubber-stamping, not testing (issue #888).

CI checks out shallow, so the control cannot read this from `git show` at run
time — hence a committed copy. Copying is safe here for the one reason it is
never safe for live code: history cannot drift. The *fixed* block is still
extracted from the real `SKILL.md`, never copied.

## Block 1 — the pre-fix scan (verbatim from `87c7434`)

Every guard the #887 fix added is absent here: no `SCAN_RC` capture, no
empty-output check, no `type == "array"` check on either side, and `null`/`[]`
defaults that make a failed state read indistinguishable from a real snapshot.

<!-- test-anchor: pmm-wake-step-4a-scan -->
```bash
CONFIG=$("$SESSION_STATE_SH" --get '.pmm.config_at_pause' 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')
FLEET_AT_PAUSE=$("$SESSION_STATE_SH" --get '.pmm.fleet_at_pause' 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')
AUTHOR=$(jq -r '.author // empty' <<<"$CONFIG")
REPO=$(jq -r '.repo // empty' <<<"$CONFIG")
REPO_FLAG=()
[[ -n "$REPO" ]] && REPO_FLAG=(--repo "$REPO")

# Lightweight scan — gh pr list only, no full per-PR gate reads
CURRENT=$(gh pr list --state open --author "$AUTHOR" "${REPO_FLAG[@]}" \
  --json number,headRefOid,mergeStateStatus --limit 500)
CURRENT_FLEET=$(jq -c '[.[] | {pr: .number, head_sha: .headRefOid, state: .mergeStateStatus}] | sort_by(.pr)' <<<"$CURRENT")
SAVED_FLEET=$(jq -c 'sort_by(.pr)' <<<"$FLEET_AT_PAUSE")
```

## Block 2 — the pre-fix decision, rendered as code

At `87c7434` the comparison was **prose**, not a fenced block:

> - If `$CURRENT_FLEET` equals `$SAVED_FLEET` (count + per-PR state) → **no-op**.
>   Print one line: `[auto-check] Fleet unchanged — re-scan continues.` Exit 0.
>   Do **not** cancel the re-scan or clear the pause marker.
> - If changed → cancel the re-scan (Step 3), then proceed to Step 4b (full
>   resume + re-launch main skill).

Below is that prose transcribed to bash, byte-identical to the compare block the
#887 fix later committed. Holding the decision half constant is what isolates
the control: every difference the run reports comes from the missing guards
above, not from a differently-worded comparison. That the decision was only
prose is itself the finding — unrunnable prose is why the fail-open shipped.

<!-- test-anchor: pmm-wake-step-4a-compare -->
```bash
if [[ "$CURRENT_FLEET" == "$SAVED_FLEET" ]]; then
  # No-op: do NOT cancel the re-scan, do NOT clear the pause marker.
  echo "[auto-check] Fleet unchanged — re-scan continues."
  exit 0
fi
# Changed (count or per-PR state): cancel the re-scan (Step 3), then Step 4b
# (full resume + re-launch main skill).
```
